name: Ketchup

pros.title: processed tomato brings a lycopene angle
pros.explanation: The USDA record contains about 12 milligrams of lycopene per 100g, and tomato processing can make the carotenoid easier to absorb.

pros.title: strong flavour can replace richer sauces
pros.explanation: A little sweetness, acidity, and tomato umami can add flavour without needing a heavy creamy sauce.

pros.title: cheap, familiar, and easy to use
pros.explanation: It is widely available, needs no preparation, and works as a quick condiment for everyday foods.

cons.title: salt stacks up quickly
cons.explanation: The USDA record contains 907 milligrams of sodium per 100g, a material tradeoff outside the visible mineral rows.

cons.title: acidity can bother reflux
cons.explanation: Tomato and vinegar make ketchup a rough fit for some people whose reflux is triggered by acidic foods.

cons.title: squeeze bottles encourage portion creep
cons.explanation: A freehand squirt is easy to underestimate when it is spread across several parts of a meal.

sourceNotes: Production-safe generic packaged ketchup entry scored as sold per 100g.
USDA SR Legacy FDC 168556 supplies the canonical catsup nutrient and amino-acid profile.
The 78% protein-digestibility value is a documented vegetable-category estimate; it describes the tiny protein amount and does not make ketchup a protein food.
Brand recipes vary materially in sugar, sodium, and tomato concentration, so this is a generic baseline rather than a claim about every bottle.

identity.basisReason: Ketchup is a packaged processed food, so the prepared state in which it is sold and eaten is the canonical per-100g comparison identity.

scoreReadiness.summary: Complete generic ketchup profile with exact USDA nutrients and amino acids plus clearly labelled starch, GI, and digestibility working values.
caveats: Protein digestibility is a documented category estimate, not an exact ketchup measurement.
Glycemic index is a contextual estimate and varies with brand formulation and serving context.
Sugar, sodium, tomato concentration, and micronutrients vary across brands.

scoreAdjustments.label: sweet condiment slop-tier penalty
scoreAdjustments.reason: A sweet condiment should not benefit too much from low fat while giving little nutrition back.
